transcript.text: Can you describe your key responsibilities and challenges as the Plant Head at the auto-components manufacturer?

I have twelve years in manufacturing and have been the plant head of an auto-components plant for the last six. About 200 people work there, and five functional heads report to me. My main work in the last two years was raising line efficiency from 71% to 82%, mostly through line-balancing and preventive maintenance. I'm applying for an executive MBA because I run the plant well but have no training in finance, pricing or strategy, which is what the next role needs.
What strategies did you implement to improve line efficiency from 71% to 82% over two years?
transcript.anchor_quote: raising line efficiency from 71% to 82%, mostly through line-balancing and preventive maintenance

transcript.text: On line-balancing, I went through the longest-cycle station first and we found that two operators were waiting for material. We moved the supply point and added a kanban card. That alone gave us about three points of efficiency.
How did you decide on prioritizing the longest-cycle station first for line-balancing, and were there alternative approaches you considered?
transcript.anchor_quote: On line-balancing, I went through the longest-cycle station first

transcript.text: I believe in empowering my people and creating a culture of ownership and excellence. We follow a continuous-improvement mindset across the shop floor, and that drives the numbers.
Can you give an example of how you empowered your team to take ownership on the shop floor, and what impact it had?
transcript.anchor_quote: I believe in empowering my people and creating a culture of ownership and excellence

transcript.text: The rejections fell from 1,800 ppm to 900 ppm in my first month as plant head. Honestly it was an easy gain and it took very little effort.
Tell me about a decision where the trade-offs were not obvious. How did you decide?
I don't know the exact share of our rejections caused by the supplier's castings. The quality head tracks that, and I haven't looked at it recently.
How did you approach preventive maintenance to improve line efficiency, and what challenges did you encounter during its implementation?
transcript.anchor_quote: raising line efficiency from 71% to 82%, mostly through line-balancing and preventive maintenance

transcript.text: I don't accept that a plant head only manages machines. Most of my day goes into people and customers. I'd ask you to reconsider the question, because I'm not an operations-only person.
How do you balance addressing both people management and operational improvements in your role as Plant Head?
transcript.anchor_quote: Most of my day goes into people and customers

transcript.text: I can't say our monthly volumes or which OEMs we supply. Those are covered by customer agreements, and I'd get into trouble.
Outside of confidentiality constraints, can you describe how you have managed customer relationships and their expectations at your plant?
I think I've answered enough for today. Could we end the practice session here? I'd like to read the feedback.

feedback.summary: The candidate demonstrated clear ownership and a strong focus on operational improvements by detailing specific actions to improve line efficiency. Their approach to empowering teams reflects leadership qualities conducive to managing large teams. However, they could improve by providing more concrete examples of decision-making trade-offs and contribute more nuanced reflections on setbacks and customer relationship management. The candidate might benefit from practicing structured storytelling to explain decisions involving trade-offs and learning from challenges, which are critical in general management roles.
